details: Expectations for a 25 basis point Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December 2026 have reached approximately 90% probability, according to prediction markets like Kalshi. This increased likelihood is largely driven by persistent inflationary pressures, with the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) for October rising more than anticipated. Higher interest rates typically increase borrowing costs and reduce liquidity in financial markets, making risk assets like cryptocurrencies less attractive to investors. While Bitcoin demonstrated resilience after the September rate hike, the continued monetary tightening expectations are likely to exert renewed selling pressure on digital assets.
title: Fed Rate Hike Odds Hit 90% Amid Persistent US Inflation

details: European Central Bank Vice President Boris Vujcic has highlighted artificial intelligence (AI) and sovereign debt as "very prominently" among the Eurozone's financial stability risks. Vujcic noted that these concerns have become more acute over the past year, with AI evolving from an equity valuation issue into a systemic concern with broader implications for debt and equity markets, cybersecurity, and operational safety. This signals a growing awareness among central bankers of the potential disruptive forces of AI and existing debt vulnerabilities.
title: ECB Warns of AI and Sovereign Debt as Prominent Financial Stability Risks

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF), in its October 2026 World Economic Outlook and related discussions, has flagged potential risks to global financial stability. These include the possibility of an AI-driven market sell-off and escalating geopolitical tensions, such as a prolonged conflict in the Middle East that could lead to significantly higher oil prices. The IMF suggests that such events could trigger market corrections in traditional finance and potentially lead to short-term sell-offs in assets like Bitcoin, as investors move away from riskier holdings.
title: IMF Cautions on AI Market Corrections and Geopolitical Risks for Global Economy

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has announced plans to enhance its oversight of banks' capabilities in assessing and managing risks stemming from climate change and nature degradation. Starting in 2027, the ECB will conduct "deep dives" into the practices of individual banks, acknowledging that while some progress has been made, "severe weaknesses" still persist in certain institutions' approaches to these emerging risks. This initiative aims to bolster the financial system's resilience against environmental challenges.
title: ECB to Intensify Bank Supervision on Climate and Nature Risks from 2027
